efficacy.judgement: Phase 1 (Rathkopf 2013) had a safety/PK primary objective, so the phase 2 nmCRPC cohort of NCT01171898 is the first primary-endpoint read. PSA response is a surrogate; SPARTAN (2018) is the outcome trial, so outcome_tested positive. Darolutamide's own model (castration-resistant VCaP xenografts, Moilanen 2015) matched ARADES and ARAMIS too. Proxalutamide's 2L mCRPC phase 3 missed interim rPFS (Kintor, tier 5) but its published preclinical work is cell lines only, so no model pairs with it; TRC-253's phase 1/2a had a DLT primary endpoint.

safety.judgement: No untested opener: the dog study (VUM00005) predates the IND (~2010) but is first public in this review, which also carries the comparison. Darolutamide ran the prediction the other way (mouse brain:plasma 0.02, no CNS signs to 46 µM) and ARAMIS seizures were 0.2% in both arms: also a match. Not scored: rash (24% vs 5.5%; idiosyncratic, not expected in tox species); QTc +12.4 ms, flagged by hERG IC50 6 µM though dog telemetry was silent, label section 12 only; hypothyroidism 8% vs 2%, rat thyroid hyperplasia only after recovery.
safety.note: Dogs convulsed at 25 mg/kg/day near human Cmax; apalutamide blocks GABA-A at clinical levels; 0.2% of patients seized in SPARTAN.
safety.short: Dog convulsions matched rare patient seizures
